input.rationale: There is no indemnity anywhere in the Agreement: the numbering jumps straight from § 19.5 (p0075) to the § 21 limitation-of-liability heading (p0076), and searches for "indemnif", "hold harmless", "defend", "infringe" and "third-party claim" return no operative indemnity — only the machinery that presupposes one (§ 9.3 relies on "the remedies required by Section 20.5", § 19.4 preserves remedies for "indemnified claims", § 21.3 makes "its indemnification obligations" an Excluded Claim, and § 30.5 preserves rights of "an indemnified party"). Vendor therefore owes us no defence or indemnity for third-party IP infringement, which is walk-away territory under this rule; there is also no Customer indemnity, so nothing to narrow. We inserted the missing Section 20 at the preferred level: Vendor defends and indemnifies Customer and its Affiliates against third-party claims for IP infringement by the Services or Deliverables, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with notice, control of the defence and reasonable cooperation, and any Customer indemnity confined to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law. We deliberately did not fall back: the fallback would have us volunteer a 3x annual-fees super-cap when § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as uncapped Excluded Claims, so the fallback's procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and cap are left for negotiation. One housekeeping point remains for Vendor to conform rather than a substantive gap: § 9.3's reference to "Section 20.5" should now point to the new Section 20.

Please also conform the dangling reference in Section 9.3 to the new Section 20.

ops.text: INDEMNIFICATION. Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. The indemnified party shall give prompt written notice of the claim, the indemnifying party shall control the defence, and the indemnified party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense. Any Customer indemnity under this Agreement is limited to third-party claims arising from Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of Applicable Law.
